evidence.quote: it only exists because the new addUnderlayRoutes subtest asserts a warning log line is absent via util_testutils.NewLogObserver; asserting no route is enough

lesson: Assert on the observable behaviour the fix changes (e.g. no route entry emitted) and do not add a log-absence assertion on top unless the log line is itself the defect being fixed. Build the test from helpers the test file and its BUILD target already use; a new import or BUILD dep that exists only for a secondary check is scope creep reviewers will ask to remove. In AVX-81794 the addUnderlayRoutes subtest pulled in util/testutils.NewLogObserver and a BUILD.bazel dep just to assert a Warn was absent, when 'no route' already proved the fix.
trigger: Planning a test for a fix whose effect is visible in output (routes, config entries, pushed protos), where you are tempted to also check that a warning/log line is gone

evidence.quote: The code comments mention ticket numbers etc (e.g. '// ... (AVX-81794): ...' in the repro test); code comments should be concise.

lesson: Keep each comment to one or two lines stating only a non-obvious why (hidden constraint, invariant); do not restate what the test sets up or asserts, and do not narrate the scenario or the other tests that cover related cases. Ticket IDs, PR numbers and 'covers the RECIPIENT side' style framing belong in the PR body, not the code. In AVX-81794 the repro test's doc comment ran 7 lines with '(AVX-81794)' and the reviewer asked for concise comments.
trigger: Writing comments or test doc comments in a repro test or fix (any stage that writes code: rca repro tests, fix-coder changes)
